newsitem.title: USA: Yurie Systems surges almost 33 pct.
newsitem.headline: Yurie Systems surges almost 33 pct.

text.p: Yurie Systems Inc jumped almost 33 percent after the market debut of the maker of asynchronous transfer mode ("ATM") products.
Shares rose four points to $16 on the Nasdaq after the initial public offering of the Lanham, Maryland company.

Shares priced at $12 each for the IPO, above their estimated pricing range of $10 to $11. That range was lifted by lead underwriter Alex Brown & Sons yesterday from its first estimate of $8 to $9 each.

Yurie's technology allows users to integrate high performance communications technology into already existing systems without scrapping all their old equipment. The systems also function with copper wire, eliminating the need for an expensive upgrade to fiber optics.
Lanham, Maryland-based Yurie sold four million shares, or about 16 percent of the company in the IPO.

The IPO scored high marks with analysts for both short- and long-term gains. IPO analysts expected Wall Street to look beyond the company's limited operating history and possibility of volatility for the next year in order to have a long-term opportunity in the company's lucrative market.
